input.question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?
input.ground_truth: The kidneys and eyes have a higher concentration of capillaries than other organs. High sugar levels in the blood cause capillary damage, thus the two are affected more. Here is an article from [_URL_3_](_URL_0_) and one from another [Reddit post](_URL_1_) in [r/diabetes](_URL_2_). Retino = eyes, Nephro = kidney, -pathy = denoting disorder in a part of the body. & #x200B; Hope that helps. & #x200B; R

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a house, and the sugar in your blood is like tiny sugar crystals. Normally, a helper called insulin lets these sugar crystals go inside the rooms (cells) of your house to give them energy.

But in type 2 diabetes, the helper (insulin) doesn’t work very well, so the sugar crystals build up outside the rooms. These extra sugar crystals can be like tiny rocks that hurt the walls of some special rooms in your house.

The kidneys and the eyes are like very sensitive rooms. The sugar crystals can hurt the blood vessels (which are like tiny pipes) in these rooms more easily. 

- In the eyes, the blood vessels can get damaged, and that’s called **diabetic retinopathy**. It can make it hard to see.
- In the kidneys, the blood vessels can also get hurt, and that’s called **nephropathy**. It can make it hard for the kidneys to clean your blood.

Other parts of your body can get hurt too, but the eyes and kidneys are extra sensitive to the sugar crystals, so they get hurt more easily. That’s why type 2 diabetes often affects the kidneys and eyes first.
